topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets out the course structure, and outlines the core learning objectives on cancer etiology.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Chance, Genetics, and Environmental Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational debate over how much cancer is driven by intrinsic biological chance and genetics versus modifiable environmental exposures.

topics.label: Oncogenic Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents and co-infections contribute to carcinogenesis, illustrated through the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: Mechanisms of DNA Damage and Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which dietary, environmental, and chemical mutagens damage DNA directly or following host metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor Promoters, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on tumor promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental windows of cellular susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying Carcinogens and Final Conclusions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro methodologies used to determine carcinogenicity, concluding with overall risk appraisal.
